BBC News | datePublished: 2026-10-24T09:44:01.854Z | dateModified: 2026-10-24T09:44:01.854Z

Seven people are missing after a multi-storey building under construction collapsed in Nairobi's Eastleigh area, Kenya, on Friday afternoon.

Dramatic footage shows the bottom floor of the block, thought to have been 16 or 18 storeys, giving way before the rest of the building crumpled, sending a plume of dust into the surrounding streets.

Dozens of builders had been working on the upper floors when it collapsed, but managed to emerge largely unscathed; those missing were thought to have been in shops that had opened at the base of the building.

Interior ministry official Kipchumba Murkomen said 66 of the 67 construction workers in the building at the time had been able to get out unharmed, while the other had suffered injuries that were not life-threatening.

The block was still under construction, with scaffolding wrapped around the outside, despite 11 shops already having opened on the ground floor. The incident has raised fresh concerns about construction standards and regulations in Kenya. Rescue workers are using cutting equipment to reach those believed to be trapped in the rubble.
